label: copy-phase input y (fed back), late in short sequences
explanation: Fires only when y is the input token during the copy phase (the model's fed-back copy of an original y). 99.9% of activations, and essentially all of the mass, are on copy-phase y inputs. It never fires in the original phase, on <DEL>, or on any other token. Copy-phase y alone gets recall 1.0 but precision 0.35, because many copy-phase y inputs stay silent. Firing is concentrated where recall_idx is 2 to 5, within the last few outputs (to_go <= 3), and in short sequences (L <= 7). It is almost silent at recall_idx 1 and in L = 8 or 9 sequences. The strongest activations (about 0.9 to 1.0 of max) occur when y is the second original token of an L=3 sequence and is fed back at the final step (pattern c y X <DEL> c [y]). Activations are weaker when y comes later and in longer sequences. The out_tok, prev_tok and first_tok identities show no meaningful selectivity.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: y, c, a, e, k, w; least: m, 2, i, l) and the token being output (most: y, r, w, s, c, e; least: o, m, p, -); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, recall_idx=4, L=3.
